messages.text: Great Britain and Ireland claim historic win in Walker Cup thriller

metadata.summary: Great Britain and Ireland won the Walker Cup for the first time since 2015 after a nerve-shredding late comeback saw them beat the USA by a  13½-12½ scoreline.
metadata.content: Walker Cup: Great Britain and Ireland produce stunning late comeback to beat USA 13½-12½ in thrilling contest | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Walker Cup: Great Britain and Ireland produce stunning late comeback to beat USA 13½-12½ in thrilling contest USA missed four putts to retain the trophy after whitewashing Great Britain and Ireland in the morning foursomes; Watch the first round of the Amgen Irish Open live on Sky Sports Golf, with coverage starting on Thursday September 10 from 1:30pm By Stephen Mills Sunday 6 September 2026 21:08, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day two of the Walker Cup held at the Lahinch Golf Club in County Clare, Ireland Great Britain and Ireland won the Walker Cup for the first time since 2015 after a nerve-shredding late comeback saw them beat the USA by a 13½-12½ scoreline. Dean Robertson's side looked to be heading for defeat after suffering a clean sweep of defeats in the Sunday morning foursomes and with the Americans three points ahead going into the singles matches. But the home side lost only two of the 10 matches and the competition eventually came down to the very last as Josh Hill won the 18th hole of his match with Tyler Watts to seal an incredible victory. The USA will be left to regret the late turnaround after four missed putts to retain the Walker Cup. Lewis Hamilton has accused Ferrari of having "no rules" after a clash with his team-mate Charles Leclerc during the Italian Grand Prix. Hamilton launched an aggressive move up the inside of his team-mate at the first corner, but was then forced off onto the gravel himself on the exit of the chicane as Leclerc held onto the inside line. Hamilton dropped from his starting position of fourth to 10th, and was left playing catch-up for the rest of the race, as he eventually finished sixth.
